evals.prompt: I'm head of product at Quaystone, we make a PR-review bot shipped as a GitHub App. It has around 340 installs and it's registered under my cofounder's personal GitHub account because that's where she created it in 2023. We want to start charging through GitHub Marketplace: $12 per repository per month as a per-unit plan, monthly only for now since annual is a pain for us. We'll probably adjust the price after a month of data, so we just want to get something live. Can you lay out the setup steps?
evals.expected_output: Transfer the app to an organization and pass publisher verification before any paid plan; GitHub describes per-unit plans as per user, so per-repository units need verification with flat-rate tiers as the fallback; monthly and annual prices are both required; published plans are immutable, so price changes mean retire-and-recreate with buyers kept on the old plan; figures flagged for verification.
expectations: States the app must be transferred from the personal account to an organization before it can sell on Marketplace
States the organization must pass publisher verification before publishing a paid plan
Names at least two publisher-verification requirements among org-wide 2FA, a verified domain, and a contact email
States that 340 installs clears GitHub's 100-installation minimum for paid GitHub Apps
States that GitHub's docs describe per-unit plans as per user but the unit label can be custom (e.g. a bundle of repositories), to confirm with the onboarding expert
Proposes a repository-bundle unit (such as per 10 repositories) or flat-rate tiers with an in-app cap
States that every paid plan needs both a monthly and an annual price
States that a published plan's price cannot be edited, only retired and recreated
States that buyers on a retired plan stay on it until they move and GitHub cannot move them
Recommends testing prices before publishing (draft listing or direct deals) rather than adjusting after launch
States that the app must handle marketplace_purchase events before approval
States that a Setup URL is required for a GitHub App to process Marketplace purchases
Marks at least one GitHub-specific figure (threshold, fee or duration) as needing verification against current GitHub docs

evals.prompt: We're Tessellate, 25 people, our GitHub App does dependency license checks. Two of our biggest prospects are a bank and an insurer, both on GitHub Enterprise Cloud and both pay GitHub by invoice. Our sales lead wants them to simply buy our paid plan on GitHub Marketplace so procurement is easy. We also want to announce Marketplace availability at our customer conference on March 18, about five weeks from now, and we haven't submitted the listing yet. How do we make both happen?
evals.expected_output: Invoiced enterprise accounts cannot buy paid Marketplace apps, so keep a direct contract path and reconcile two entitlement sources; GitHub publishes no review time and practitioners report multi-week waits, so do not promise Marketplace availability on the date; launch the unlisted app with own install button and announce it as coming to Marketplace.
expectations: States that invoiced enterprise accounts cannot purchase paid GitHub Marketplace apps
Recommends a direct contract or off-Marketplace purchase path for the bank and the insurer
Says the app must reconcile entitlements from both Marketplace and direct contracts per account
States that inside an enterprise only an enterprise owner (who is also an org owner) can purchase Marketplace apps
States that GitHub publishes no review duration or SLA for app listings
Says practitioners report review waits from about three weeks to over two months without reply
Advises against committing to Marketplace availability on March 18
Recommends launching with an unlisted app installed from the vendor's own site or install button
Suggests announcing the listing as pending or coming to GitHub Marketplace rather than live
Warns against clicking Withdraw request or resubmitting to speed up review
Recommends a GitHub Support ticket after several weeks of silence, filed under Billing or Account since the form has no Marketplace category
States that a paid listing adds a financial onboarding phase after review that can stall for weeks

evals.prompt: Ferrocline here, we sell an infrastructure drift scanner and ship ferrocline/scan-action as our GitHub Action. Our org already has the blue Verified badge on its GitHub profile since we verified our domain, so we're verified on Marketplace, right? A big customer says their enterprise only allows actions from GitHub and verified creators and ours gets blocked. Also we're moving the action repo to a new ferrocline-oss org next week, and finance asked whether we can put a price on the action itself on Marketplace.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the org Verified domain badge from the Actions verified creator badge (partner program via GitHub partnerships), explains the verified-creators policy and the per-action allowlist workaround, warns the transfer drops the verified creator badge unless the new owner is verified, and states actions carry no Marketplace pricing.
expectations: States that the organization profile Verified badge is different from the Marketplace verified creator badge for actions
Says the verified creator badge is requested from GitHub partnerships or the Technology Partner Program
Explains that the customer's 'Allow Marketplace actions by verified creators' policy blocks actions from creators without that badge
Offers the workaround that the customer's admin adds an explicit allowlist entry for the action (owner/repo pattern)
Warns that transferring the action repository drops the verified creator badge unless the new owner is a verified creator
States that a repository transfer keeps the Marketplace listing and a redirect for existing workflows
States that actions cannot carry a price on GitHub Marketplace
Recommends monetizing the product the action calls instead of the action
Does not claim the org Verified badge satisfies the verified-creators Actions policy
Does not route the user to publisher verification as the fix for the action badge

evals.prompt: Our backend lead at Lanternfish (GitHub App for test flake detection, already listed on Marketplace with a Free and a Team plan at $40/org/month) wrote this billing plan and I want a second opinion: 1) we update the customer's plan whenever a marketplace_purchase webhook arrives, that's our single source of truth; 2) when someone downgrades from Team to Free we cut Team features the moment we get the downgrade click; 3) on cancellation GitHub uninstalls the app so we don't need to do anything; 4) QA will test upgrades by buying the Team plan on our live listing with a company card and refunding it. Anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: Webhooks are not redelivered so add periodic sync against the plan accounts endpoint; downgrades take effect at the end of the cycle via effective_date, pending_change arrives first; GitHub does not uninstall on cancellation, so downgrade to free, and on full cancellation deactivate, revoke token, delete data within 30 days; never test on the live listing, use a separate public dev app with a draft listing.
expectations: States that GitHub does not resend failed marketplace_purchase webhook deliveries
Recommends periodic reconciliation against the list-accounts-for-a-plan endpoint
States that downgrades take effect at the end of the current billing cycle, not at the click
Mentions effective_date as the field that tells when the change applies
Mentions the pending_change event that announces a scheduled downgrade or cancellation
States that GitHub does not uninstall the app when a paid plan is cancelled
Says a cancelled paid plan should fall back to the app's free plan
Lists cancellation duties: deactivate the account, revoke the OAuth token, delete customer data within 30 days
Rejects testing purchases on the live listing
Recommends a separate public development app with a draft listing for purchase tests
Notes that purchases on published plans in a draft listing are not charged
Mentions the Apply Pending Change developer feature (or equivalent) to force pending downgrades during tests

evals.prompt: Bramblework sells a code-coverage SaaS on our own website with Stripe, $20/seat. Our GitHub App has about 150 installs and we want to put it on GitHub Marketplace as free-only so we get discovery but keep all billing on Stripe. Separately our AI team wants to list our Copilot Extension in the Copilot category of the Marketplace next month. Which listing should we do first?
evals.expected_output: GitHub bans or limits a free-only listing for a product sold outside Marketplace (150 installs also clears the 100-install paid gate), so a free-only listing is a review risk and a paid plan is likely owed and needs org publisher verification; Copilot Extensions were retired on 2025-11-10 and the category removed, so build an MCP server instead.
expectations: Flags GitHub's rule against a free-only Marketplace plan for a product sold outside Marketplace as a review or rejection risk
States that 150 installs exceeds the 100-installation paid threshold
Concludes a Marketplace paid plan would be owed, not a free-only listing
States paid plans require an organization owner and publisher verification
Offers the unlisted public app installed from the vendor's site as the alternative that keeps Stripe billing
States that GitHub retired GitHub App-based Copilot Extensions (November 2025)
States the Copilot Extensions Marketplace category no longer exists
Recommends an MCP server as the replacement for the Copilot Extension
Mentions GitHub's 5% fee on Marketplace sales
Ranks the listing options or states a recommended order rather than listing them flat

evals.prompt: Pebblecart is shutting down its GitHub App Pebble Insights at the end of this month. It's listed on GitHub Marketplace with about 60 paying orgs on monthly and annual plans. Plan: click delist today, delete the GitHub App registration on Friday, and delete our own action pebblecart/insights-action repo too so nobody uses it. What do we need to watch out for?
evals.expected_output: Delisting is immediate but subscriptions run to cycle end and the app cannot be deleted before then; the Developer Agreement asks 30 days written notice and continued support and refund terms for existing buyers; deleting the action repo deletes the listing and frees the name for anyone, so delist the action by unchecking publish on each release instead.
expectations: States that existing subscriptions end at the end of their current billing cycle after delisting
States the app cannot be deleted until the current billing cycle ends
Mentions the Developer Agreement's 30 days written notice for removing a listing
States support obligations to existing buyers continue after delisting
States that refund terms are the vendor's responsibility, not GitHub's
Flags that annual-plan buyers run until their cycle ends, beyond the end of the month
Warns that deleting the action repository frees the Marketplace name for anyone to claim
Recommends delisting the action by unchecking Publish on every published release
Recommends archiving the action repository instead of deleting it
Recommends a dated message to paying customers
